question.prompt: Last summer \(30 \%\) of the birds living on Town Lake were geese, \(25 \%\) were swans, \(10 \%\) were herons, and \(35 \%\) were ducks. What percent of the birds that were not swans were geese?

solutions.explanation:
The requested percentage uses the birds that are not swans as its whole. These birds account for
\[
100\%-25\%=75\%
\]
of all the birds. All the geese belong to this group.

Because the given percentages refer to the same original total, that total cancels when we divide. The percentage of non-swans that are geese is therefore
\[
\frac{30}{75}\cdot100\%=40\%.
\]
The answer is \(40\%\), choice C.
solutions.title: Use the non-swans as the whole
